verdict.rationale: Authy documents an encrypted cloud backup intended for when you lose your phone. Tokens are decrypted on new devices with your password, and new devices can be added via SMS, voice, or existing-device approval. A hands-on report confirms a user regained access after their phone was pickpocketed, though another user lost their tokens on a phone upgrade after assuming they would port automatically, which suggests backup must be deliberately enabled. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party step-by-step recovery documentation (evidence is feature-page one-liners), and clarity that backup is opt-in rather than automatic.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: Use our backup feature incase you lose your phone. We encrypt your data, and only decrypt on the devices using a password only you know.
Encrypt your 2FA data and backup to our cloud, without storing passwords with us.
Add new devices with SMS, voice or existing device approval.
This was tested when their phone was pickpocketed in Amsterdam. They find Authy fine for this use.
